purpose: Define Topic membership as explicit semantic classification/grouping: every canonical tree node belongs to one or more Topics or is explicitly classified as outsider.

semantics.purpose: Define Topic membership as explicit semantic classification/grouping: every canonical tree node belongs to one or more Topics or is explicitly classified as outsider.

semantics.classification_rule: Every machine-significant canonical node has at least one Topic membership unless explicitly outsider.
semantics.multiplicity_rule: A node may belong to multiple Topics simultaneously.
semantics.grouping_rule: Topic membership groups semantics for recursive reading and traversal; it does not imply containment, ownership or authority.
semantics.locality_rule: Topic declarations belong with the semantic node/subtree whose material they group rather than in a mandatory separate Topic directory.
semantics.question_rule: When adding semantics, first ask whether it belongs under an existing Topic; create a new Topic when no existing Topic expresses the grouping cleanly.
semantics.abundance_rule: Topic count is not artificially minimized; semantic readability takes precedence.
semantics.recursive_rule: A generic reader can recursively discover Topic membership from canonical nodes.

invariants.rule: Every machine-significant canonical node is classified by explicit Topic membership or explicitly marked outsider; Topics may inherit and compose other Topics.

hard_gates.condition: canonical node has neither Topic membership nor outsider classification
